records.current_summary:
South Atlantic island settlement with its own assembly: same-sex activity legal since 1989, equal age of consent since 2005, and full equality in April 2017 when the assembly approved same-sex marriage and civil partnerships 7-1, on a public consultation showing 90 per cent support for marriage and 94 per cent for partnerships — the registrar confirmed the law the following June, adoption followed the same year, the constitution bans sexual-orientation discrimination, and the first Pride was held in the capital that April. An official of the community described it as 'open, tolerant and respectful'; note that the much more remote dependencies administered from the same capital did not follow on marriage.

The earlier profile's inherited arithmetic and its borrowed UK custody stories have been deleted: on the surviving evidence the legal picture here is stronger, not weaker, than the administering state's, and there is no source indicating the GB single-sex-services code extends to the territory.

prison_adds.title: LGBTQ rights in the Falkland Islands (Wikipedia; Prisons Ordinance 2017 equal-treatment clause)
prison_adds.summary: Thin: Wikipedia's 'LGBTQ rights in the Falkland Islands' article documents no trans-prisoner housing data for the territory - no birth-sex vs identity placement policy, no special units, no solitary/segregation practice - but its hate-crime section notes that the Prisons Ordinance 2017 (legislation.gov.fk, in force 2019-07-17) requires prison staff to treat all prisoners equally without distinction to, among other categories, sexual orientation; a statutory equal-treatment clause covering prison staff, with no trans-specific placement or segregation detail.

records.current_summary:
A self-governing Crown Dependency with its own parliament, Guernsey moved briskly through the 2010s: in 2011 it aligned blood-donation rules with the metropole, ending the HIV-era ban on gay and bisexual donors; in June 2015 the states rewrote the adoption law to open adoption to same-sex couples, removing a fifty-year bar on unmarried couples; and in December 2015 the states approved same-sex marriage 37-7, rejecting civil-partnership and secular-union alternatives as insufficient, with the law itself commencing from spring 2018.

That record covers sexual orientation squarely; the position on gender identity was asserted in the earlier profile without any cited source and has been deleted, so a transgender visitor should treat legal gender recognition and trans-specific protection as unestablished here — the more notable local quirk being that, on the documented chronology, civil partnership arrived later than in the neighbouring dependency that shares the island group's institutions.

prison_adds.title: Guernsey Prison - Wikipedia
prison_adds.summary: Wikipedia article on Guernsey Prison (Les Nicolles), the island's only prison: opened 1989, 11 wings, capacity 139, operated by the States of Guernsey and accommodating male, female and vulnerable prisoners of juvenile and adult ages (population ~99 in November 2024). Contains no birth-sex-vs-identity housing rule, no trans special unit, and no solitary/segregation practice for trans prisoners; verdict thin: no usable finding on the prison-housing axis.

records.current_summary:
Isle of Man: a self-legislating Crown Dependency in the Irish Sea whose parliament, Tynwald, works through its own bills on these questions. The House of Keys in 2005 proactively adopted a clause protecting employees from dismissal over sexual orientation, framing it in human-rights terms; the chief minister publicly committed to marriage equality in 2015, at a time when this parliament and Northern Ireland's assembly were the only British legislatures refusing it; the Marriage and Civil Partnership (Amendment) Bill passed its final legislative stages in April 2016 and the first civil partnership was converted to marriage that July, preserving the couple's 2015 wedding date.

Current reference material confirms the settled picture: civil partnerships from 2011, marriage since 2016, and a legal gender-recognition right in force since 2009 alongside 'gender reassignment' protections in island equality law. Claims about the metropole's single-sex code and its statutory guidance were carried in the earlier profile without primary legislative support and have been deleted, leaving the local record as the basis of this entry.

prison_adds.title: Isle of Man Prison - Wikipedia
prison_adds.summary: Wikipedia article on Isle of Man Prison (Jurby), the island's only functioning prison (GBP 41.7m facility at the former RAF Jurby, fully operational 14 August 2008), operated by the Isle of Man Prison Service. Documents separate units for remand and convicted prisoners, female prisoners, young offenders and vulnerable prisoners, plus a segregation unit - but no birth-sex-vs-identity placement rule, no trans special unit, and no trans-specific solitary/segregation practice; verdict thin: no usable finding on the prison-housing axis.

records.current_summary:
A US territory: the federal anti-trans turn of 2025–26 (document/marker rules, TSA screening friction) applies in full — and unlike some territories, local law compounds rather than softens it. In July 2025 Puerto Rico's governor signed the most severe ban on gender-affirming care in the United States, criminalising provision of hormones or surgery to anyone under 21 even with parental consent — up to 15 years' imprisonment, $50,000 fines, loss of medical licences, with parents potentially exposed; civil-rights groups announced court challenges, and the signatory had campaigned presenting as LGBTQ-friendly.

Local politics have swung both ways: the island's marriage ban was dismantled in the federal courts after local couples sued (2014), while religious-freedom and conversion-therapy bills advanced in 2019 before the governor withdrew them under organised pressure. For a trans visitor today: federal paperwork friction, the country's harshest local care-crime regime, and a visible advocacy community pushing back in court.

prison_adds.title: Executive Order 14168 ("Defending Women from Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government") - Wikipedia
prison_adds.summary: Executive Order 14168 (signed 20 January 2025) directs US federal agencies, including the Bureau of Prisons, to recognize only two sexes, and federal practice has followed by placing transgender inmates in facilities congruent with their sex assigned at birth rather than their asserted gender identity. The ACLU said it had received reports that transgender women were being transferred to men's prisons, told they would be, or moved to solitary confinement, and the Bureau of Prisons stopped reporting the number of transgender people it holds. Advocates say the order violates the Prison Rape Elimination Act's requirement that trans inmates' housing be decided on an individual safety assessment. Federal custody rules apply in Puerto Rico as a US territory; the search found no separate Puerto Rico Department of Corrections trans-inmate housing policy, special unit, or ruling.

records.current_summary: Assessed comparatively protected (low-risk tier, July 2026) — but the state rose in risk after the University of Maine system capitulated to national pressure on trans sports participation rather than defending its trans students and athletes: the system affirmed compliance with the new national rules once the national agriculture department suspended its funding (March 2025). Direction: better than the country overall, with an upward risk signal.

prison_adds.title: Inmate at women's prison files suit over housing of transgender prisoner (Sun Journal, Maine)
prison_adds.summary: Sun Journal (3 Apr 2026, Mark LaFlamme) documents that Maine Corrections housed Andrea Balcer, a 27-year-old transgender woman and convicted double murderer, in the women's facility (Maine Correctional Center, Windham) for at least a year as of April 2026 - i.e. placement by current gender identity rather than birth sex. Inmate Katie Mountain (41) filed a 30-page complaint on 3 Apr 2026 against MDOC Commissioner Randall Liberty, Warden Ben Beal and Balcer, alleging chronic harassment and assault by the trans prisoner; attorney Cynthia Dill filed it. Outcome pending (complaint filed, no ruling reported in the article); the harassment/assault claims are allegations, while the placement fact - a trans woman held in the women's prison - is documented.
